title: Dropped Work Does Not Count
eyebrow: Landed and running on your board; the outside reader has not signed it off yet

actions.fyi: Nothing is waiting on you. Override any decision below if you disagree with one.

content.label: What you asked
content.lead: You saw bw-oio5 sitting under Cancelled and asked whether dropping a piece of work drags the whole job with it, and said dropped work should not count towards the total.

rows: Did cancelling a sub-task cancel the epic?
No. An agent cancelled that epic itself, as a duplicate. Cancelling a piece never moves the job.
Should dropped work count towards the total?
It no longer does. That was a real fault, and it ran deeper than the one number.
Were those sub-tasks cancelled in error?
The cancelling was right; the copying was not. Filed as its own card for the job that caused it.

content.label: What it cost you
content.lead: A job with nothing left to do could never reach a hundred, and the button that lets you sign one off appears at a hundred and nowhere else.

blocks.text: The last row is the point: jobs with real work left read exactly as they did, so the number now means what it says.

content.label: What the board looks like now
content.lead: The same card, before and after.

after.caption: The counts that count, and what was dropped said out loud

content.label: What else was wrong behind it
content.lead: An outside reader went over the change three times and turned it down twice; every point it raised was real.

rows: A job with every piece dropped read as finished
It offered you the sign-off on a job where no work happened. It reads as nothing done now.
Dropped cards drawn as the live work
Five abandoned pieces looked like the outstanding work, under a count saying there was none.
The card and its panel gave one job two sizes
Two screens, two answers, same job.
Only one of eleven themes said what was dropped
On Linear Minimal and Notion Warm a full bar sat over a longer list with no explanation.
Three separate copies of what blocks a piece
All three had to be taught the same thing in step; the one that got missed would have gone quietly wrong.
Every card rebuilt a lookup of the whole board
A fresh 421-entry map of the whole board per card, for roughly 180 cards, every time the board redraws.

content.label: What stops it coming back
content.lead: The rule now lives on the one list of states, and two checks hold it.

rows: 171 unit cases
Put the old rule back and eight go red, on numbers taken from bw-oio5's own shape.
A check that drives a real browser at your board
It compares every job card on screen with what the board holds. Green today; run with the old rule it names all three jobs that dropped anything.

blocks.text: The screen check exists because no test that stops at the code could have caught this: the board looked calm and drew the wrong number.

decisions.title: Dropped work leaves the job's size entirely
decisions.why: Your words. A job of fourteen with four dropped is a job of ten, and it finishes when those ten are done.

decisions.title: A job whose every piece was dropped reads as nothing done, not as finished
decisions.why: The reader turned down my first answer here and was right: no work happened, so it is a job to drop, not one to sign off.

decisions.title: Your running app was rebuilt and restarted
decisions.why: The fix is a number on your screen; it was not delivered until your own copy showed it.

decisions.title: The duplicated cards were left to the job that made them
decisions.why: bw-oio5.11 to .14 sit here cancelled beside the fresh copies of themselves. That belongs to the move job, which is running.

next.if_nothing: The reader finishes its reading and the job closes, or it raises more points and I answer those the same way.
